correctness.rationale: A cyclic orientation string has missing edges exactly at transitions (B_i,B_{i+1})=(0,1); M has mean np(1-p), P(M=0)=p^n+(1-p)^n and P(M=1)=n∑_{j=1}^{n-1}p^j(1-p)^{n-j}. Any spanning-tree edge set omits exactly one edge, so symmetric difference >=|M-1|. Uniformly deleting a missing edge, or any edge for M=0, is rotation-equivariant and has uniform tree marginal; equality holds pointwise. Therefore W1=E|M-1|=npq-1+2(p^n+q^n), and TV=1-P(M=1) because the M=1 component is uniform and other components disjoint. For p=λ/n, rare ones form asymptotic isolated transitions, M→Poisson(λ); exact formulas yield f(λ)=λ-1+2e^-λ and TV=1-λe^-λ. Convexity gives unique minimizers log2 and 1; finite-p optimizing sequences cannot stay nonsparse by W1 bound and exponential P(M=1) bound. The edge metric is unnormalized, including n=3 and p endpoints.
